content.title: About
content.content: Tuna is a marine predatory fish of the Scombridae family, found in warm and temperate ocean waters. Raw tuna has a firm, slightly pink flesh with a mild flavor and moderate fat content. It is commonly used in sushi, sashimi, steaks, and also canned after cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna can migrate thousands of kilometers, moving between tropical and temperate zones.
The largest species, the bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus), can exceed 600 kg in weight.
Tuna is rich in protein and omega‑3 fatty acids, making it popular among athletes.
In Japan, tuna is a prized delicacy with centuries‑old fishing traditions.
Tuna can maintain a body temperature higher than the surrounding water thanks to a specialized circulatory system.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Raw tuna provides EPA and DHA, which support heart health, vascular function, and brain development.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Tuna supplies all essential amino acids, beneficial for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many meat products, tuna contains little saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna is a good source of B12, B6, and niacin, which aid energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The fish provides selenium, magnesium, and phosphorus, important for antioxidant protection and bone health.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Large tuna species can accumulate mercury; pregnant women and children should limit consumption.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including tuna.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw fish can harbor pathogenic bacteria; using fresh product and proper hygiene is essential.

items.title: Storage issues
items.content: Improper storage leads to rapid quality loss, off‑odors, and off‑flavors.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw tuna is ideal for sashimi, rolls, poke bowls, and salads. It is sliced thinly and often served with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger. It can also be lightly marinated in citrus or vinegar before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh tuna in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, tightly wrapped in a sealed container or film. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C using vacuum‑sealed packaging. Thaw frozen tuna in the refrigerator, not at room temperature, before use.
